1. This database includes operating coal mines producing 1 million tonnes per annum and more, with smaller mines included at discretion, and proposed coal mines with a capacity of 1 million tonnes per annum and more
2. This database includes a separate sheet specifically for documenting coal mines that closed mainly since 2015. ("Closed Mines" sheet)
3. For more information on each mine, with references, see GEM.wiki pages (here) ("Non-Closed Mines" sheet, Column H, I)
4. For an explanation of the compilation of this data, see "Methodology" on Global Energy Monitor Wiki platform (GEM.wiki) (here)
5. For coal mine employment estmates, see "Estimating coal mine workforce size" on Global Energy Monitor Wiki platform (GEM.wiki) (here)
6. For summary statistics by province, country, region, company etc., see "Summary Statistics" on Global Energy Monitor website (here)
7. For links to reports using GCMT data, see "Reports" on Global Energy Monitor website (here)
8. A mapping tool for this data is available on the Global Energy Monitor website (here)

9. For more information on mine ownership check out the Global Energy Ownership Tracker: The tracker maps each level of the chain from the direct owner (as in, the lowest-level identified owner in the chain of ownership) up to their highest-level ultimate parents (e.g., corporations, investment firms, and governments). Ownership links are reported with the percentage of ownership, including owners that have controlling interest as well as those with minority, non-controlling interests (if over a threshold of 5% ownership). Companies IDs, such as PermIDs, are also included.

10. Where appropriate, Global Coal Mine Tracker (GCMT) assets have been associated with individual remotely-sensed methane plumes described in the Global Methane Emitters Tracker (GMET). Plumes are associated with a mine asset if the origin of the plume, as determined by the satellite data provider, appears to fall within the boundary of a GCMT asset upon manual review by a GEM researcher. This manual review involves visual inspection of basemap imagery in Google Earth Pro as well as RGB imagery (for CarbonMapper plumes) from the time of the plume emission, and analysis of government and media sources related to the mine as detailed in the GEM wiki pages for individual GCMT assets. Note that the GMET does not include every known remotely sensed methane plume – see the GMET methodology page for information on data coverage.

11. This dataset is an update to the version released in May 2025, featuring major revisions to the "Parent Company" column, which now reflects the latest GEM ownership format and includes associated Entity IDs for parent companies (excluding Chinese parent companies). Another key update is the inclusion of wiki page URLs for the mine assets added in this release. For other additional changes between the May 2025 release and May 2025 v2 release, please refer to the "Change Log" tab for details.

About.Column2: Definition
"Status" describes the various active/inactive stages of a coal mine or mine project.
A coal mine where coal removal is occurring for commercial purposes. This includes mines that have produced coal within the year, even if operations were temporarily suspended for several months.

A coal mine project that has not yet begun operation. This includes projects that have been announced (via corporate or government planning documents), projects that are under permitting (including feasibility studies), projects that are under construction, as well as those in test operation.
A coal mine that is neither operating nor retired, such as those that are idled or put on "care and maintenance." Such mines could return to operation, but are not currently operating.

A proposed coal mine project for which a cancellation announcement has been made by the owning company or government authorities. GEM also assigns a status of "cancelled" to projects when no progress has been observed for 4+ years.
A proposed coal mine project for which no public updates nor progress has been observed for 2+ years.
A previously operating coal mine that has been permanently closed.

"Status detail" describes the mine status on a granular level, such as which planning stage a proposed coal mine project has progressed to, or whether an operating mine is experiencing temporary work stoppages.
A status assigned when a coal mine project has been described in corporate or government plans, but full details remain unknown.

A status assigned when the economic viability of a coal mine project is being explored. During the exploration stage, information is gathered about a potential mine site's characteristics via geological surveys, pre-feasability studies, and the drilling of boreholes.
A status assigned when permit applications (environmental assessments, land use rights, water licenses, etc.) for a coal mine project have been filed, but not yet obtained.
A status assigned to a coal mine project that has been granted permit approvals, but has not yet begun construction.
A status assigned when a coal mine project has begun construction of its mining infrastructure and facilities.
A status assigned when a coal mine project begins coal removal, but not yet for commercial purposes.

A status assigned when an operating mine temporarily closes, but there is potential to recommence operations at a later date. During the care and maintenance period, coal production stops but the mine site is still managed by minimal staff to ensure it remains in a safe and stable condition.
A unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to each coal mine by GEM for internal identification purposes.
A unique numerical identifier assigned to each US coal mine by the US Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) for identification purposes nationwide.
The geographic country or area where a coal mine or proposed coal mine project is located.
The name of a coal mine or proposed coal mine project.
The nickname or alias of a coal mine or proposed coal mine project. AKAs are often used with proposed projects which have not yet been assigned an official name.
The non-english name of a coal mine or proposed coal mine project, as it appears in the official language of the country or area where the mine is located.
The name of the larger mining complex or group to which one or more coal mines belong.
The URL corresponding to a coal mine's or proposed coal mine project's english GEM wiki page.
The URL corresponding to a coal mine's or proposed coal mine project's non-english GEM wiki page.
Refers to the type of coal mine project: expansion, extension, or new.
A "new" mine is a greenfield mine planned to be developed in an area where there was no previous mining activity.
An "expansion" is when an existing mine seeks to increase its existing coal capacity.
An "extension" is when an existing mine seeks to mine new areas to extend its mine life.
Refers to proposed coal mine projects that will be developed in stages, often with initial development followed by subsequent expansions over time (e.g., Phase I, II, III).

The immediate owner of a coal mine or coal mine project who is responsible for the mining of the coal. The number in brackets next to the owning entity's name denotes the percentage of shares they hold. If an individual rather than a company owns the mine, this is indicated by the term "natural person(s)."
The non-english name of the immediate owner of the coal mine or proposed coal mine project, as it appears in the official language of the country or area where the mine is located.

The highest-level owner of a coal mine or coal mine project. The number in brackets next to the owning entity's name denotes the percentage of shares they hold. If an individual rather than a company owns the mine, this is indicated by the term "natural person(s)."
The geographic country or area where the parent company is headquartered in.
Unique identifier assigned by the GEM's Global Energy Ownership Tracker team.
The maximum amount of coal a mine or mine project is engineered to produce, expressed in millions of tonnes per year.
The amount of coal produced by a mine, expressed in millions of tonnes per year.
The year during which the cited coal production occurred. (If coal output for the current year is unavailable, data for the most recently available year is given.)
The amount of coal produced by a US mine, expressed in millions of short tons per year. This value applies to US coal mines only.
The classification of coal mines by mining method, including "Surface," "Underground," and combined "Underground & Surface" facilities.
The specific technique used to extract coal from the earth.
also known as “Open Cast”, refers to mining directly on the ground surface
is a type of surface mining where the overlying vegetation, rock, and soil (overburden) is removed in order to reach the underlying coal seam, which usually lies a few feet beneath the surface.
is a mining practice where the tops of mountains are removed, exposing the seams of coal. It is a form of surface mining at the summit or summit ridge of a mountain.
also known as “Room and Pillar”, it’s a method of underground mining. In this method, seams of coal are mined partially, leaving large pillars of coal intact to support the overlying layers of rock
is a type of underground mining method used to extract coal from a seam that is too deep for open-pit mining
More than one mining method.
The total surface area of the mining covered by the coal mining operation, including surface facilities, access roads, overburden dumps, and the underground or open-pit mine footprint.
The vertical distance from the ground surface down to the coal seam that is being mined.

Indicates the confidence level in the reported depth of the coal mine. "Exact" means the depth is directly stated in a reliable source, while "Estimated" means it is inferred from averages at the national level in a variety of industry and government reports.
About.Column3: For more details, please refer to GEM’s methodology wiki page on estimating methane emissions from coal mines.

About.Column2: The total number of personnel employed by a coal mining operation, including those directly involved in extraction and those supporting operations.

Indicates the accuracy level of workforce data. "Exact" means the workforce size is explicitly reported in data sources, while "Estimated" refers to figures generated using GEM’s machine learning model when official data is unavailable.
About.Column3: For more details, please refer to GEM's wiki page on estimating coal mine workforce size.

About.Column2: The classification of coal based on its physical and chemical properties, particularly its carbon content, calorific value, moisture, volatile matter, and ash content. Global Coal Mine Tracker use British coal type (lignite, subbituminous, bituminous, anthracite).

The classification of coal based on its primary use:
-Thermal Coal: Used for power generation or industrial heating.
-Metallurgical Coal (Coking Coal): Used for steelmaking and other industrial processes.
The proportion of metallurgical coal within the "Thermal & Met" classification under Coal Grades for opearting coal mines.
The proportion of thermal coal within the "Thermal & Met" classification under Coal Grades for operating coal mines.

Indicates the confidence level in the accuracy of the information provided. A percentage split is marked as "Exact" when it is explicitly stated in the data source, and "Estimated" when it is based on the researcher’s interpretation or experience drawn from available sources.
The year in which the percentage breakdown of coal grade was reported or deocumented.
The combined amount of economically recoverable or minable coal.
About.Column3: Please see GEM's wiki on coal reserves for details.

About.Column2: The year in which the total coal reserves of the mine were reported or evaluated.
The total estimated volume of a coal deposit in the ground
A measure of how long a coal reserve will last at the current annual rate of production.
The year when the mine commenced its commercial operations.
The year in which the coal mine is scheduled to close or has already ceased operations.
The expected operational lifespan of a mine, expressed in year, based on the currently known and economically recoverable reserves, and the planned annual production rate.
The year in which the life of mine is reported or evaluated.
Coalfield to which a coal mine belongs.
Location of the project expressed in decimal degrees, assumed to use the WGS84 coordinate system (as in Google Maps).
Location of the project expressed in decimal degrees, assumed to use the WGS84 coordinate system (as in Google Maps).

Indicates whether the location is "Approximate" or "Exact". Location is "Approximate" based on using nearest city or inferred from contextual information in the data source. Location is "Exact" when explicitly provided in the source materials.

The main end user or receiving entity of the coal produced by the mine. This may include coal power plants, steel plants, export terminals, or industrial facilities that rely on coal as a primary source.
The name of the end user or receiving entity of the coal. The project name should match exactly with those documented by GEM to ensure consistency.

The gas-level rating of a coal mine is a classification system that indicates the methane content and gas-related risk level of a coal mine.
About.Column3: In this release, this indicator is available only for coal mines in China, where mines are typically classified into three levels: Low-gas, High-gas, and Outburst. For a detailed explanation of the methodology, please visit the wiki page here.

About.Column2: The year in which the gas-level rating of the coal mine was appraised or officially reported.

About.Global Coal Mine Tracker - May 2025 v2: Reported Coal Mine Methane Emissions (thousand tonnes per year)
About.Column2: The amount of methane emissions from a coal mine reported by an official source or company reports, expressed in thousands of metric tonnes per year.
About.Column3: Column name changed from "Reported Coal Mine Methane Emissions (thousand tonnes  CO2e)" to "Reported Coal Mine Methane Emissions (thousand tonnes per year)"

About.Global Coal Mine Tracker - May 2025 v2: Year of Reported Coal Mine Methane Emissions
About.Column2: The year in which the coal mine methane emissions were reported or released.
The identifier assigned by the reporting agency to the coal mine associated with the reported methane emissions.

A “Yes” in this field indicates that the GCMT asset has been associated with a remotely sensed methane plume detailed in the Global Methane Emitters Tracker. Yes* refers to the one mine (Mandalong Coal Mine) which had methane plumes associated with it in the December 2024 briefing which were not included in the version of GMET public at the time due to minor differences in query methodology.
About.Column3: Some mines may have multiple plumes from different dates/times of observation associated with them. See the wiki page for each GCMT asset for details and download the full Global Methane Emitters Tracker here.

About.Column2: A “Yes” in this field indicates that the GCMT asset has been associated with a known coal mine methane mitigation project (e.g., pre-mining drainage, flaring, ventilation air methane destruction, utilization, etc.).
About.Column3: Some mitigation projects span multiple mines, and some mines are associated with multiple mitigation projects. See this companion dataset for more details, and methodology wiki page here.

About.Global Coal Mine Tracker - May 2025 v2: GEM Coal Mine Methane Emissions Estimate (MCM/yr)
About.Column2: An estimate of annual methane emissions from a coal mine calculated by GEM, expressed in million cubic meters per year (MCM/yr). This estimate is based on the Model for Calculating Coal Mine Methane (MC2M).
About.Column3: Due to limited production data for Chinese coal mines, CMM emissions are estimated using the latest annual capacity utilization rate—72.8% for the coal mining and washing industry—as reported by the National Bureau of Statistics of China in 2024.

About.Global Coal Mine Tracker - May 2025 v2: GEM Coal Mine Methane Emissions Estimate (M tonnes/yr)
About.Column2: An estimate of annual methane emissions from a coal mine, expressed in million metric tonnes per year.
An estimate of coal mine methane emissions, expressed in carbon dioxide equivalents (CO₂e) over a 20-year time horizon.
About.Column3: Starting in 2022, the Global Coal Mine Tracker adopted the latest conversion factor from the IPCC’s Sixth Assessment Report (2022), using a 20-year Global Warming Potential (GWP) of 82.5.

About.Column2: An estimate of coal mine methane emissions, expressed in carbon dioxide equivalents (CO₂e) over a 100-year time horizon.
About.Column3: Starting in 2022, the Global Coal Mine Tracker adopted the latest conversion factor from the IPCC’s Sixth Assessment Report (2022), using a 100-year Global Warming Potential (GWP) of 29.8.
